items.note: Thirty participants did concept generation with GPT-4 agents versus with a human partner (brainstorming and TRIZ) in two phases a month apart; creative-thinking performance (fluency, elaboration, originality) and EDA measured; below 50 participants and assignment not stated.

Sixteen groups of five brainstormed with DALL-E or Miro, online or offline, in a 2x2 design; two raters scored fluency, elaboration, flexibility and originality; assignment method and whether the tool factor was within or between groups not stated.

Two preregistered studies: Study 1 compares ChatGPT-4 slogans with human slogans (quality and diversity), Study 2 gives people GenAI assistance on slogan writing and finds quality gains for less creative people; abstract taken from the PsyArXiv version (doi 10.31234/osf.io/uz2cm), same work as the SSRN record.

Framed field experiment in which innovation teams used a custom GenAI ideation tool or worked as a control group; idea quality, speed and idea diversity compared; the arXiv abstract gives neither N nor randomization (search notes report 70 students in 24 teams, randomly assigned, per the Mendeley dataset).

Scenario-based between-subjects experiment with 226 designers varying creative control in designer-AI co-creation, with mediation through ownership and cognitive load; check whether design creativity is rated on output or self-reported, and whether a scenario counts as producing output.

Ten in-person workshops (54 participants) evaluated AI interventions for team brainstorming in AI impact assessment; AI improved assessment quality for one use case but not another; comparison condition, assignment, and how quality was scored are not detailed.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page); per search notes, compares GAI-assisted and traditional teaching in logo concept ideation for novice and skilled students, with GAI raising quantity, novelty and diversity of concepts; N and assignment unknown.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, ScienceDirect blocked); per a search snippet, Experiment 1 (N = 170, figure unverified) varied whether students thought independently before or after collaborating with AI on a creative problem, a comparison of AI configurations with creativity outcomes.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Springer page); per search notes, a two-month course with an AIGC group (n = 54) versus traditional methods (n = 59), creativity scored pre and post on the Creative Engineering Design Assessment; groups may be intact classes, and whether the post-test was done without AI is unknown.

Mixed-methods classroom study in a college creativity course scoring AUT fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality to assess the effect of ChatGPT-3 on divergent thinking (search notes: AUT without technology, then about a month later with ChatGPT, a non-randomized within-person comparison); N not stated.
